R package Stem · technical note

Model verification against the reference papers

Every equation of the STEM model, its EM algorithm, its kriging predictor and its parametric bootstrap, checked line by line against the three companion works of Fassò and Cameletti that define it. The core is faithful. One defect was found, in a branch of the likelihood evaluation, and fixed.

Package Stem 2.0.0 Scope STEM core, not the SC-STEM layer Result 1 defect found and corrected

How the three papers relate

They build on one another; only one is the direct reference

WorkRoleRelation to the package
Fassò, Cameletti, Nicolis (2007)
Environmetrics 18, 245–264		 The geostatistical dynamical calibration (GDC) model, the most general of the three: instrument calibration with an additive bias A(t) and a multiplicative bias B(t), loadings from empirical orthogonal functions, heterogeneous networks mixing gravimetric and TEOM monitors. The package implements the special case with no calibration bias.
Fassò, Cameletti (2007)
GRASPA Technical Report n. 27		 The three-stage hierarchical model with covariates, the EM algorithm, and the spatio-temporal parametric bootstrap. The direct reference. It announces this package by name: “Software availability: R package Stem — Developer: Michela Cameletti”.
Fassò, Cameletti (2010)
Simulation 86, 139–153		 The fullest published statement: the same model and EM, plus the kriging predictor, the bootstrap and a sensitivity analysis of the model components. Its Equations (12)–(21) are what the estimation code implements.

The model itself is the three-stage hierarchy

Z_t = X_t beta + K Y_t + e_t e_t = omega_t + epsilon_t Y_t = G Y_{t-1} + eta_t eta_t ~ N(0, Sigma_eta)

with a measurement error epsilon that is white in space and time, a spatial component omega that is white in time but correlated in space, and a latent temporal process Y_t shared by the network through the loading matrix K.

The defect

filterstep, univariate branch

The mean of the one-step-ahead predictive distribution is, by Equation (9),

mu_t = X_t beta + K y_t^{t-1}

so the regression term is added to the state contribution. The multivariate branch of filterstep does exactly that. The univariate branch subtracted it:

/* before */ z - (f - XXXcov %*% betacov) /* after */ z - (f + XXXcov %*% betacov)
Why it had gone unnoticed

The branch is reached only when a fit has a single location, which essentially never happens for a pooled model over a monitoring network. A clusterwise algorithm changes that: every cluster is a fit in its own right, and a small cluster is reachable. The defect would have produced a silently wrong log-likelihood — and therefore wrong information criteria and a wrong cluster assignment — rather than an error.

Consequence for the spatially-clustered layer

Why the SC-STEM assignment score rests on solid ground

The label update of SCSTEM_Estim ranks clusters by a per-location conditional pseudo-likelihood whose variance is sigma2eps + sigma2omega. Equation (7) of the technical report justifies that value exactly:

Sigma_e[i,i] = sigma2omega * Gamma(0) = sigma2omega * (1 + gamma) = sigma2omega + sigma2eps
In short

The spatially-clustered extension is built on the correct covariance structure of the original model. What it cannot inherit is an exact per-location decomposition of the likelihood: the spatial covariance couples the locations, so the assignment score has to be a pseudo-likelihood. That is a property of the spatio-temporal specification, and it is why the alternating algorithm is not globally monotone — see ?SCSTEM_Estim.
